title: arXiv Mathematics — Daily notable papers (16 October 2026)
global_caveat: This is an inferred research-significance shortlist, not an official arXiv trending chart. Citation momentum is not meaningful for this very recent batch and no independent discussion signal was established.

sections.title: On exponential sums with multiplicative coefficients
sections.abstract: For multiplicative coefficients and an additive phase close to a rational with denominator in the stated range, the paper proves optimal leading constants in exponential-sum bounds; complete multiplicativity improves the constant, and related conjectures receive counterexamples.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 proves a uniform bound with leading constant 4/√6 for 1-bounded multiplicative functions and 1 for completely multiplicative functions, both optimal, under the stated rational-approximation and denominator hypotheses (arXiv abstract and HTML introduction).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: |f(n)| ≤ 1; α is within 1/(qx) of reduced a/q; q ≤ x/((log x)^2(log log x)^3). The coefficient is completely multiplicative for the improved constant 1.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp theorem is range-dependent; it does not establish the same constants for arbitrary denominators or all analogous sums over smooth numbers.

sections.title: A counterexample to the generalized Viterbo conjecture on the spectral distance in a disc cotangent bundle
sections.abstract: The authors prove unboundedness of the Lagrangian spectral distance under topological and geometric assumptions on the closed base manifold, disproving a generalization of Viterbo's conjecture, and classify the surface cases where it holds over Z₂.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 proves unbounded spectral distance for Lagrangians Hamiltonian-isotopic to the zero section under the stated hypotheses; the abstract also reports a classification of all surfaces for which the conjecture holds over Z₂.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed connected R-orientable Riemannian manifold with a metric without conjugate points, H¹(M,R) ≠ 0, and Euler characteristic nonzero in R.
sections.unique_caveat: The disproof is conditional on these hypotheses; it does not decide the conjecture for every closed manifold. Surface classification is specifically over Z₂.

sections.title: The rank problem for metric spaces
sections.abstract: The paper constructs a complete, second-countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank, answering a question of Fokina, Friedman, Körwien and Nies and showing that the known upper bound ω₁ is sharp.
sections.claimed_result: The author constructs a complete, second-countable metric space with uncountable Scott rank and develops a Baire-category variant used to reprove known rank bounds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete, second-countable metric space; Scott rank in the descriptive-set-theoretic setting.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives the existence result and application but not enough construction detail to assess how explicit or canonical the example is; proof not independently checked here.

sections.title: The Hopf conjecture with T³-symmetry
sections.abstract: The authors prove positive Euler characteristic for closed even-dimensional manifolds of positive sectional curvature that admit an isometric three-torus action, and extend the result to orbifolds.
sections.claimed_result: Every closed even-dimensional manifold with positive sectional curvature and an isometric T³ action has positive Euler characteristic; the authors prove the analogous result for orbifolds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed, even-dimensional, positive sectional curvature, with an isometric action by a 3-torus; corresponding orbifold result.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a symmetry-restricted case; it does not settle the Hopf conjecture without the T³-symmetry assumption.

sections.title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process
sections.abstract: The paper characterizes when minimal eigenvalues of interchange-process Laplacians on two Specht modules are comparable independently of edge rates, gives an inverse-polynomial comparison bound in those cases, and derives mixing-time consequences.
sections.claimed_result: In comparable cases, the paper establishes an inverse-polynomial lower bound for the rate-independent comparison constant and obtains unconditional mixing-time bounds for interchange and exclusion processes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Interchange-process Laplacians on Specht modules, comparisons uniform over edge rates.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed universal constant 2/3 is a conjecture, not a proved theorem; the abstract does not state explicit unconditional mixing-time bounds.

sections.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
sections.abstract: The authors develop a perturbation theory for minimal submanifolds with strongly isolated singularities and give a criterion for their persistence across open sets of background metrics, including examples from spherical suspensions of Veronese embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a “sporadic persistence” criterion and produce families of continuously varying stationary varifolds with isolated singularities observable on an open set of metrics.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Varying background Riemannian metrics; strongly isolated singularities. Examples are spherical suspensions of Veronese embeddings associated with normed division algebras.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated examples concern specific suspensions in spheres of dimensions 4, 7, 13 and 25; the abstract does not imply persistence for general singular minimal submanifolds.

sections.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
sections.abstract: The authors establish an integral equivariant crepant-transformation correspondence for a binary-dihedral surface quotient, extend it to all genera and full descendants, and apply it to a degree-zero orbifold GW/DT correspondence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Iritani's integral form of the equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture for the minimal resolution of C²/BD₄ₙ, then use Givental quantisation to prove the all-genus full-descendent version and deduce a degree-zero orbifold GW/DT correspondence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The specific quotient is C²/BD₄ₙ for the binary dihedral group, with C×-equivariance; application to [C²/BD₄ₙ] × C.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract treats this type-D quotient setting; it does not claim the same result for arbitrary quotient singularities or groups.
